chunks: And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Do not lease the land in exchange for dates, wheat, barley, water shares, or surplus water."
I said, "And what are the arbīʿāʾ?" He said: "It is the water share, and nīṭāf is surplus water. But you may take it on lease for gold, silver, one-half, one-third, or one-quarter."

key_terms.التَّمْرِ: dates used here as a prohibited form of rental payment
key_terms.الثُّلُثِ: one-third share as a permitted contractual proportion
key_terms.الذَّهَبِ: gold as a permitted medium of payment
key_terms.الشِّرْبُ: a water share or irrigation allotment
key_terms.الْأَرْضَ: the land being leased for cultivation
key_terms.الْحِنْطَةِ: wheat used here as a prohibited form of rental payment
key_terms.الْفِضَّةِ: silver as a permitted medium of payment

ai.seo_question: What forms of payment are permitted or prohibited when leasing agricultural land in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding leasing agricultural land, prohibiting certain forms of payment such as produce and water-related rights. It permits leasing instead for gold, silver, or specified fractional shares, indicating regulated forms of agricultural contracting in fiqh.
